name: Sprinklr
description: Sprinklr is a unified customer-experience platform for social media management, customer care, listening, marketing, research, and digital engagement. Its governance model applies customer roles and workspace access across a broad set of REST APIs.
agentUseSummary: Add a customer-owned Sprinklr API key, OAuth access token, exact environment, and primary workspace binding, then let agents verify identity-redacted governance status through one fixed endpoint.

credentialRequirements.name: SPRINKLR_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Sprinklr API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use the API key from the customer's Sprinklr Developer application. Relay encrypts it and sends it only in the Key header.

credentialRequirements.name: SPRINKLR_ACCESS_TOKEN
credentialRequirements.label: Sprinklr OAuth access token
credentialRequirements.helpText: Supply the current customer-authorized bearer token. Relay encrypts it and never exposes it to agents.

credentialRequirements.name: SPRINKLR_ENVIRONMENT
credentialRequirements.label: Sprinklr environment
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use production for app.sprinklr.com or the exact prodN environment for the customer instance.

credentialRequirements.name: SPRINKLR_WORKSPACE_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Sprinklr primary workspace ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Paste the exact positive-decimal primary workspace ID returned by Sprinklr's Me API.

capabilities.label: Read governance status
capabilities.description: Verify that the customer token resolves in its exact environment and primary workspace while returning only a safe user-role type and binding booleans.

approvalRequired.label: Get Sprinklr governance status
approvalRequired.description: Verify the exact primary workspace binding and return only a safe user type plus customer/workspace binding booleans, excluding names, emails, IDs, properties, and broader platform data.

blocked.label: Access identity or governance detail
blocked.description: Names, emails, user IDs, customer IDs, workspace IDs beyond the exact bound value, properties, roles, permissions, teams, clients, users, and governance configuration are blocked.

blocked.label: Access content, profiles, or analytics
blocked.description: Social accounts, profiles, messages, cases, comments, assets, campaigns, dashboards, listening, reporting, research, customer-care data, content, authors, URLs, media, and analytics remain blocked.

blocked.label: Publish, write, or administer Sprinklr
blocked.description: Drafting, scheduling, publishing, messaging, engagement, case changes, profile changes, imports, exports, webhooks, credentials, user management, and administration remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw API or bulk access
blocked.description: Arbitrary environments, paths, methods, queries, bodies, workspace overrides, pagination, polling, raw responses, bulk operations, browser sessions, and undocumented endpoints remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The bounded governance-status read requires approval; identity, content, profiles, analytics, publishing, writes, administration, raw APIs, pagination, bulk, and export remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same bounded read runs directly; exact environment/workspace binding, fixed endpoint, redaction, response caps, audits, and provider governance remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw receives one fixed Sprinklr governance-status wrapper with exact environment/workspace binding and identity redaction.
Hermes receives the same fixed Sprinklr governance-status wrapper with exact environment/workspace binding and identity redaction.

providerSetup.blocker: Sprinklr API access requires an Enterprise entitlement, a developer application/API key, a platform user with Generate Token permission, environment/workspace authorization, and a current OAuth token.
providerSetup.nextAction: The customer creates or selects its own Sprinklr application, authorizes the exact environment/workspace, supplies the current API key and access token, and completes a live read-only check.

evidence.supports: Sprinklr documents REST/JSON APIs, OAuth 2.0, mandatory Bearer and API-key headers, environment-specific authorities, and user-level governance.
Official setup documents customer application registration, environment-specific API keys/tokens, workspace selection, the fixed GET /api/v2/me call, and its identity-rich response.
Official API reference documents GET /api/v2/me with Bearer authentication; Relay returns only safe governance status and verifies the exact workspace binding.
Sprinklr states that API use requires an Enterprise license, a Sprinklr seat or authorizing user, the correct instance environment, a developer application, API key, and OAuth authorization.

Platform terms restrict licensed modules to customer internal use, require compliance with connected-service rules, and prohibit API redistribution; Relay exposes no raw or redistributable Sprinklr API surface.

securityNotes: The customer API key and OAuth access token are encrypted as secret references and sent only in Key and Authorization headers to the fixed api3.sprinklr.com host.

Relay accepts only production or a syntactically safe prodN environment, verifies the exact positive-decimal primary workspace returned by /api/v2/me, and never follows environment or workspace values from provider content.
The connector allowlists only GET /api/v2/me, rejects redirects, caps responses at 1 MB, and returns only userType, primaryWorkspaceConfirmed, and customerBound.

Names, emails, user/customer IDs, properties, roles, permissions, social profiles, content, messages, cases, listening, analytics, reporting, publishing, writes, administration, arbitrary APIs, pagination, bulk, and export are excluded.

Provider 401/403/429 and server errors are surfaced safely; OAuth application creation, consent, token capture, refresh-token rotation, and provider-console work remain customer/external acceptance steps.
